title: Oklahoma National Guard responds to wildfires in Western Oklahoma - Package
description: PACKAGE - The Oklahoma Office of Emergency Management requested aerial and ground firefighting support from the Oklahoma Army National Guard. The historic fire conditions burned nearly 400,000 acres in Western Oklahoma as of April 15, 2018.
keywords: Oklahoma National Guard, Wildfire, brush pumper, Okla_wildfires_April_2018, Chinook, Black Hawk, firefighting

transcript.text: - [Announcer] Oklahoma National Guard's
Joint Operations Center has been responding
to requests from the Office of Emergency Management
as Oklahoma has seen historic wildfire conditions
sparking the burning of nearly 400,000 acres
in western Oklahoma as of Sunday afternoon.
On Friday, a black hawk and chinook helicopter
dropped buckets of water
providing aerial fire fighting support.
On Saturday, the Oklahoma National Guard
was on the ground delivering nearly 9,000 gallons of water
to the fire fighters on the front lines
via four trucks called hippos
that carry 2,000 gallons each.
- Again this is something that we haven't done before,
it's pretty precedent for us to get ground forces
on the ground to support these fires.
We've heard great things that we're supporting
the effort there and they're able
to fight the fires quicker than they have in the past.
- [Announcer] While the hippo vehicles
remain working in the field,
two black hawk helicopters and numerous personnel
are on standby heady for the call.
Reporting for the Oklahoma National Guard
from Mooreland, Oklahoma,
I'm Army Staff Sergeant Christopher Bruce.
